directive: Valerius continues the expedition and leads his men in disciplined loose phalanxes, maintaining enough spacing for movement between units, coordinated protection of different parts of the column, and an outward-facing perimeter while the investigation of the engineered road and its unexplained administrative status continues.

events.title: VALERIUS REFORMS THE COLUMN INTO DISCIPLINED LOOSE PHALANXES
events.body: Before the column resumes its work, Valerius reorganizes the men into disciplined loose phalanxes rather than keeping them packed into one continuous mass. The intervals between the units are deliberate, allowing men to move from one part of the column to another without breaking the whole formation. The outermost men are instructed to face outward, away from the interior, so that the perimeter remains attentive to movement approaching from the surrounding country while the men inside the formation remain free to support whichever section requires them. The arrangement is rehearsed before the expedition proceeds, with the rear, flanks, and forward edge each receiving attention rather than allowing the whole column to look only in the direction of travel. The scribes record the formation as an operational practice accompanying the expedition rather than as a change in the permanent army establishment. No new soldiers are recruited or detached.

events.title: THE LOOSE FORMATION ALLOWS THE SURVEY PARTY TO PROTECT THE ROAD INVESTIGATION WITHOUT HALTING ITS WORK
events.body: The new arrangement proves useful when the expedition returns to the surveyed corridor. Men from the outer portions can shift toward another section without forcing the entire column to close ranks, while the outward-facing perimeter continues watching the approaches around the working party. The scribes are therefore able to inspect drainage cuts and the blocked side approach while the surrounding men maintain coordinated observation. The formation does not establish that an enemy or hidden population is present; it is a precaution arising from the unresolved question of who has used and maintained the road. The road remains unclaimed as to builder, date, and final destination, while the expedition's ability to investigate it without bunching the column becomes a recorded field practice.

events.title: THE OUTER WATCHES NOTICE SIGNS OF RECENT PASSAGE WITHOUT FINDING THE PEOPLE WHO MADE THEM
events.body: During the outward-facing watch, men on the eastern side of the column notice disturbed vegetation and recent-looking impressions near a secondary section of the route. The signs are insufficient to identify the travelers who made them, and the party finds no camp, armed group, or settlement at the end of the visible trace. The formation allows the men nearest the observation to move inward and report the finding without leaving the opposite side of the column unwatched. The scribes mark the signs as a fresh investigative lead rather than evidence of deserters or a marooned community. The discovery increases the reason to inspect the route carefully, but it does not establish the identity or number of the people responsible.

events.title: THE PRIVATE DISPATCH TO CELER IS COPIED INTO THE EXPEDITION'S CONFIDENTIAL REGISTER
events.body: The expedition scribes make a controlled copy of the private dispatch already sent toward Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer. The copy preserves Valerius's distinction between observed roadwork and the unproven possibilities of deserters, fugitives, or an isolated community. No reply has arrived, and no new Roman order is attached to the correspondence. The confidential copy is kept apart from the ordinary route register so that the field evidence cannot be mistaken for the hypothesis communicated to Celer.

events.title: THE FORMATION MOVES BETWEEN SECTIONS OF THE COLUMN WITHOUT BREAKING THE OUTWARD WATCH
events.body: Valerius spends the day testing the formation over uneven ground along the engineered corridor. The loose phalanxes retain enough spacing for men to move between neighboring units, allowing a threatened or uncertain section to receive additional observers without collapsing the column into a tight block. The men at the outer edge continue facing outward while those inside the formation remain available to shift toward the front, rear, or flanks. The practice makes the column less dependent on a single direction of attention and gives Valerius greater control over the distribution of his men while the expedition remains in unfamiliar country. No battle occurs and no enemy is identified; the development is a disciplined operational refinement of the expedition already underway.

events.title: THE ESTATE ADMINISTRATION CONTINUES WHILE THE EXPEDITION REMAINS AWAY
events.body: At the estate, the stewards continue the established watering arrangement with the nearby smallholders while ordinary administration proceeds without a new land transfer or payment. The household remains separate from the expedition's investigation and receives no new report that changes the established holdings. Agriculture remains at its recorded maximum, and no new financial realization is established by the week's administrative activity.

events.title: THE COLUMN ENDS THE WEEK IN A DEFENSIVE CAMP ARRANGEMENT WITH THE OUTER WATCH FACING AWAY FROM THE INTERIOR
events.body: The expedition closes the week at a temporary position beside the investigated corridor. Valerius keeps the loose phalanx arrangement as the column settles, with the outermost men facing outward and the interior left open enough for movement between units and rapid reinforcement of any section. The arrangement is maintained as a precaution rather than a response to a confirmed enemy. The route investigation remains active, the signs of recent passage remain unexplained, and the private dispatch to Celer has not yet produced a reply. With supply already at zero, the expedition does not claim a further advance beyond what can be supported by the existing position; the next stage will require careful logistical judgment.
